front: The five Project Management Focus Areas
back: Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling, Closing.

front: Former name of the Focus Areas
back: Process Groups. Same five names.

front: Are Focus Areas the same as phases?
back: No. Focus Areas are groupings of management actions. All five can occur within each phase, and they overlap.
Actions to define a new project or phase, often including formal authorization to start.

front: Four things that happen in Initiating
back: Initial scope defined; initial funds committed; stakeholders identified; project management roles assigned.
Project charter and stakeholder register.
Projects are authorized only when aligned with strategic objectives, with business case, benefits and stakeholders considered from the start.
Documents that originate outside the project and are inputs to it: the business case and the benefits management plan.
Actions that establish the intended scope, define and refine objectives, and develop the course of action to reach them.
Ongoing refinement of the plan as more information becomes available. Planning is iterative.
Brief, high-level up-front planning used in highly iterative approaches, followed by frequent replanning.
Planning near-term work in detail and later work at a high level, adding detail as it approaches.
The collection of knowledge and artifacts describing the course of action. The authoritative reference for how the project will be managed.
Actions to complete the work consistent with the agreed course of action: coordinating resources, engaging stakeholders, performing activities.
Actions to track, measure, review and regulate progress and performance, identify needed changes and initiate them.
Monitoring: collect, compare and report performance. Controlling: analyze variances, assess trends, recommend corrections.

front: When does Monitoring and Controlling take place?
back: In parallel with all other Focus Areas, throughout each phase and the whole project.
Actions to formally complete or close a project, phase or contract, or to terminate a project early.
That outputs, outcomes and benefits were achieved, and that the work of the other Focus Areas is complete.

front: Do the Focus Areas apply to agile projects?
back: Yes. They are independent of approach and industry. In adaptive work they are revisited in every iteration.

front: Can the project management plan change during executing?
back: Yes. It can and should change whenever that would enhance the project's value.
